text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan Muslim League led by Nawaz Sharif has swept the national and provincial assemblies and is set to form a two-thirds majority government at the centre and Punjab.
- The PML President Nawaz Sharif said his party "was committed to improving relations with India".
- Pakistan renewed its pledge to support the 50-year-old struggle of the people of Kashmir against Indian occupation.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said though elections results have been engineered, she will give a chance to Nawaz Sharif to complete his tenure.
- Five women, including ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto and her mother, won National Assembly (lower house) seats in Monday's elections.
- World media appeared stunned with the size of the Nawaz Sharif victory and Benazir Bhutto's devastating defeat in Pakistan's fourth elections in eight years, marred by a dismally low turnout.

- Business leaders expressed hope that a Nawaz Sharif government would settle the business community's long unresolved matters, specially pertaining to taxes and development of infrastructure facilities.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange gave an enthusiastic welcome to the overwhelming win of Nawaz Sharif as the post-election session saw the 100-share index gaining another 52 points.
- PML leader Nawaz Sharif said economic revival would be his government's first priority.

- Pakistan may be unable to meet the IMF target of cutting its budget deficit to four percent of gross domestic product by June, said Sartaj Aziz, who is widely expected to become the next finance minister.
- The United States has congratulated former Pakistani premier Nawaz Sharif on his electoral victory and pledged to work with him to improve bilateral ties.
